subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

options: The body's cells not responding to insulin
The kidneys failing to filter glucose
The pancreas not producing enough (or any) insulin
questions.explain: In Type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.q: The relay neurone is found mainly in the:
questions.explain: Relay neurones are located in the CNS and connect sensory neurones to motor neurones.

options: Cause an egg (in a follicle) to mature in the ovary
questions.explain: FSH, secreted by the pituitary gland, stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries and triggers oestrogen release.

questions.q: Which part of the eye changes shape to focus light on the retina?
questions.explain: The lens changes shape (accommodation) to focus light from near or distant objects onto the retina.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: A muscle or gland that produces the response
The receptor that detects the stimulus
The relay neurone in the spinal cord
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: At a synapse, how is the signal passed from one neurone to the next?
options: The neurones touch and pass electricity directly
The impulse jumps as a spark
questions.explain: At a synapse, neurotransmitters diffuse across the gap and trigger an impulse in the next neurone.

questions.q: In dim light, the pupil reflex causes the:
options: Pupil to get larger to let more light in
questions.explain: In dim light radial muscles contract and the pupil widens to let more light reach the retina.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: How does auxin cause a shoot to bend towards light?
options: Auxin stops all growth on the lit side
Auxin destroys cells on the shaded side
Auxin builds up on the lit side, making it grow faster
Auxin builds up on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and increases cell elongation there, bending the shoot towards the light.

questions.q: Reflex actions are described as automatic because they:
options: Are controlled consciously by the brain
Do not involve the conscious areas of the brain
questions.explain: Reflexes are automatic and rapid, not involving conscious thought, which helps protect the body.
